Game 1 (Sweden) and Game 4 (Poland) are the clearest calls on form, motivation and opponent fragility. Games 6, 9 and 11 carry meaningful volatility due to injury crises and form reversals — treat those as doubles territory at best.

predictions.analysis:
This is the decisive Group B4 fixture — Sweden secure promotion to Nations League A with a win, while Bosnia play for second place. The context could not be more sharply drawn, and Sweden arrive carrying the momentum of an UP-FORM tag and a home record of two wins from two in this campaign. Viktor Gyökeres is the story the continent is following, and UEFA have flagged his scoring run as the central narrative heading into Solna.

The structural case for Sweden is reinforced dramatically by Bosnia's defensive injury crisis. Tarik Muharemović is SUSPENDED and Dennis Hadžikadunić is confirmed out through injury — that is both first-choice centre-backs missing for a team about to face one of Europe's most potent club strikers. Replacement-quality matters enormously here: whoever fills in at the heart of Bosnia's defence will be improvised, poorly drilled as a partnership, and facing a forward line that ripped Romania apart 3-1 at this venue. Sweden's season xGA of 0.59 per game — an extraordinary figure — tells you they are built to control matches defensively as well as dominate offensively.

The reverse fixture finished 1-1 in Sarajevo, which the market will cite as evidence of Bosnia's resilience. But that was away from home, with both CBs fit, and without the added motivation pressure on Sweden of claiming top spot on home soil. Bosnia's xG data exposes their fragility further: their xGF of 0.89 in the last five games versus 1.20 actual goals suggests they have been marginally outscoring their chances — regression risk coming into a match where they will spend long periods defending. Sweden's home xGF of 1.69/g dwarfs that.

The only note of caution is that Wålemark is unavailable on the wing, slightly narrowing Sweden's attacking width, and Bosnia — when organised and compact — can grind out low-scoring results. The 0-0 away at Poland and the draw in Sweden in September show they know how to absorb pressure. But with two CBs out, and Sweden's motivation at its highest, the home win is the clearest call on this coupon.
predictions.value_note: 1.52 is short but justified given the injury context — Bosnia's defensive lineup is genuinely unknown.
